# Security Report

`mxcli report security` is a model review that says what protects the data, what
does not, and what to fix — instead of a score. The scored `mxcli report` can rate an
app 0/100 almost entirely from intended row-level rules while the real problems are
elsewhere; this page puts those rules in a table with a verdict each and lists the
real findings first.

It is not a penetration test. Hosting, headers, Marketplace CVEs and rate limiting
are out of scope, and the page says so.

## Run it

```bash
mxcli report security -p app.mpr --format json -o docs/security/sec.json
mxcli report security --from docs/security/sec.json --annotations docs/security/status.yaml -o docs/security/security.html
```

## Triage a client-callable flow

The page lists every microflow a user role may call that takes a persistent object.
The client passes that object as a **plain id**. Work through each one:

1. **Does it take the acting user (or "me") as a parameter?** Then any user the
   caller may read can be substituted. Measured on a running app: a subscription was
   created for another user this way. Fix: derive the user in the body
   (`$currentUser`), never take it from the page.
2. **Does it check the caller in its own body?** (`$currentUser`,
   `[%CurrentUser%]`) — then it holds, provided the check is on the object it acts on.
3. **Entity access off and it writes?** Nothing stops a substituted id. Turn entity
   access on or add the check.
4. **Relies on access rules?** Then it is as safe as the parameter entity's read
   rule for the granted roles. `all` means any id works.

**The parameter-versus-association rule** decides which flagged flows are real: an
object *parameter* is a plain id and can be substituted, but a forged *association
value* in a request is rejected by the runtime ("Hash is invalid"), and with strict
mode `mx.data.get` is refused. A flow that only receives objects through
associations of an object it already checks is not exposed the same way.

## Unsafe defaults

- **A constant whose default looks like key material** (base64 of 16/32 bytes, hex
  keys, PEM) is committed in git with the model. "Override in every environment" in
  a comment is not a control. Empty the default, set it per environment, and
  **rotate the key** — it is in the history.
- **Test switches defaulting to true** (`MockDataOn = true`) switch on mock imports
  or relaxed checks in any environment that forgot the override.
- **Demo users at Production**, including the app template's `demo_administrator`.
  Two runtime facts decide the fix: dropping a demo user from the model does **not**
  delete its account from an existing database, and the runtime does **not**
  reactivate a demo account that was deactivated. Deactivate the accounts in each
  database as well as removing them from the model.

## Live probes (only on a local app, only undone through the app)

To confirm a flagged flow, replay its page action with a substituted object id on a
local app with demo users (`mxcli run --local`), see whether it is accepted, then
**undo the effect through the app** (the same flow, or the UI) — never by editing
the database behind the runtime's back. Never probe a shared or production
environment.

## Statuses

```yaml
items:
  "finding:constant-secret:Crypto.EncryptionKey": {status: fixed, note: "rotated 2026-11; env only"}
  "finding:flow:Swaps.ACT_Subscribe": {status: open, note: "takes $Medewerker from the page"}
  "flow:Admin.ACT_Reset": {status: intended, note: "admin only, checks role in body via SUB"}
  "rule:CONV007": {status: intended, note: "reference data and admin roles"}
  "rule:SEC010": {status: accepted}
```

Statuses: `open`, `fixed`, `accepted`, `intended`, `real`. A finding marked fixed
that the next run still finds stays listed with its status — re-measure after fixing.
